name: Whistle melodies accurately
blurb: Pucker whistling in tune is a small ear-training project: your mouth is an instrument you cannot see, so the only feedback loop is your ear.
gear: A piano or keyboard app for reference pitches
steps: Find a comfortable middle-range note and hold it steady for ten seconds against a tuner.
Learn to bend up and down a semitone at a time, checking against the tuner.
Whistle a major scale up and down, correcting each note against a keyboard.
Whistle simple melodies you know well, and record them to check the intervals.
Expand your range at both ends, gently — the top of the range needs a tighter pucker and less air.
Whistle along with recordings, which trains pitch matching in real time.
tips: Tongue position controls pitch far more than lip shape does. Think of the vowel sounds “oo” for low, “ee” for high.
Dry lips are the enemy. Keep them moist.
proof: You whistle a full melody in tune, verified against a tuner or a recording.
